The bug is on the `if (!note)` line. It selects `owner_id` but never compares it to `req.user.id`, so anyone logged in can add tags to someone else's note, and the 201 vs 404 also tells them the note exists. The fix is `if (!note || note.owner_id !== req.user.id)` so it returns the same 404 for missing and not-yours.

The primary key on `(note_id, name)` means a note can't have the same tag twice, and the cascade deletes a note's tags when the note is deleted, so nothing is left orphaned. `INSERT OR IGNORE` makes adding a tag a second time harmless instead of a 500. Yes, I turn on `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` in `src/db.js` next to the WAL setting, so the cascade does run. I'd still check it's on the same connection the routes use. An unauthenticated `GET /nonexistent` gets a 401, not a 404, because the tags router is mounted at `/` and its `router.use(requireUser)` runs for any path that reaches it, before Express would fall through to the 404. Order matters because anything mounted after the tags router is behind auth, so `POST /login` has to be registered before it or nobody could log in.

I'd want tests for the tag name rules first: upper-case gets lower-cased, and anything outside `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$` or longer than 32 characters gets rejected, so bad names can't get in. Next is the ownership check, where user B posting a tag to user A's note must get 404 and write nothing. Then adding the same tag twice should leave one row, which guards the `INSERT OR IGNORE` and primary key behaviour. I'd also test that deleting a note removes its tags, which guards `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` being lost. Last, `GET /tags` should count only my own tags, and an unauthenticated request should get 401, so a mount-order change doesn't expose anything.
